title: Statistical Review of World Energy 2026
notes: 2025; printed pp. 33, 47 and 81 (PDF pp. 34, 48 and 82). Global crude/condensate and gas output and definitions. Statistical compilation, not a well-level audit or company revenue dataset. Gas is standardised at 40 MJ/m³ GCV and excludes flared/recycled gas; annual growth is leap-year adjusted.

title: ExxonMobil Guyana begins production at fourth offshore Guyana project
notes: Event on the same date; opening, ONE GUYANA and ownership paragraphs. Supports startup, initial annual-average target of 250,000 b/d, installed capacity above 900,000 b/d at startup, and 45/30/25 interests. Company disclosure; targets and capacity are not full-year actual output.

publisher: Government of Guyana Department of Public Information
title: First oil achieved at Guyana’s fourth FPSO ONE GUYANA
notes: Same-day event; first five body paragraphs. Government announcement corroborates first oil and SBM construction and describes licensing/decommissioning safeguards. The government is a stakeholder; this is not independent proof of returns or environmental performance.

title: FPSO ONE GUYANA Purchase by ExxonMobil Guyana Completed
notes: Same-day event; first three paragraphs. Approximately US$2.32bn cash consideration, ownership transfer and operations/maintenance through 2035. Consideration is neither total field-development cost nor SBM annual revenue.

title: Form 8-K dated July 18 2025
notes: Same-day event; Item 8.01. Confirms completion of the Hess acquisition and wholly owned subsidiary status. Establishes ownership change, not realised synergies.

title: Products and services
notes: Product catalogue at access date; Reservoir Characterization, Well Construction, Production, and Plug and Abandonment. Supports business categories, not rankings or particular customer contracts.

title: Oil production
notes: Business description at access date; grades and integrated upstream/downstream paragraphs. Supports production and processing-related positioning. Some page figures are dated 2023; no cost, emissions or capacity ranking is adopted.

title: Annual Letter to Shareholders 2026 About us
notes: Liquids Pipelines, Gas Transmission and Midstream, and Gas Distribution and Storage sections. Supports transport, storage and distribution roles; throughput shares are not used as upstream production shares.

title: About us
notes: At access date; About us text and business navigation. Supports independent E&P positioning and activities. Independent is a business classification, not absence of joint ventures or gas commercial activities; no self-reported ranking is adopted.

title: The Implications of Oil and Gas Field Decline Rates Executive summary
notes: Opening section and no-investment scenario. Supports the estimate that nearly 90% of upstream investment since 2019 offset declines. Model and historical-sample analysis, not every company’s spending mix or an oil-price forecast.

title: Oil Market Report October 2026
notes: Public Highlights and Fragile rebound; 2026 forecast and September estimates. Uses 100.7 mb/d supply and 102.4 mb/d demand forecasts to frame risk. This broader oil balance differs from S01 crude/condensate; do not splice the series for growth calculations.

title: Impacts of Middle East conflict set to reshape energy investment plans as disruptions put focus on security
notes: Oil/gas investment paragraphs; 2026 forecast. Supports oil investment below US$500bn, gas investment of US$330bn and supply-chain constraints. Broader supply infrastructure is included; these are not E&P revenue or pure upstream capex.

title: Global Methane Tracker 2026 Key findings
notes: Opening and mitigation-policy sections; 2025 estimates. Oil 45 Mt and gas 36 Mt of methane across their activity scopes, not E&P alone. Combines measurement, satellite and inferred data; not a globally measured census.

title: Natural gas explained Natural gas prices
notes: Commodity cost, Transmission and distribution costs, and regional price factors. Supports separating fuel and transport costs and the effect of pipeline capacity. US explanatory material, not a single global gas price.
